_README: Residue of the con-copy sweep (detect_con_copy.py), classified BY DIRECTION.
The flag fires when our con slot equals our std slot while an independent source says the
two differ. That says a cell is wrong; it does NOT say WHICH slot holds the error. The
direction is decidable with no PDF at all:
our stored value == screener's CON  -> our con is right, the STD slot holds the copy
our stored value == screener's STD  -> our std is right, the CON slot holds the copy
Splitting the 16 open cells this way on 2026-08-09 gave 6 con-copy, 9 mirror, 1 neither --
not the 11-plus-5 the previous pass recorded. Four cells booked as 'no confirmable
consolidated column' were mirror cells all along: read_con_copies only opens pages whose
own wording says CONSOLIDATED, so for a mirror cell it is filtered away from the very
statement that holds the answer. It was never going to find them. The reader now takes
--basis std for that direction.
SKFINDIA IS BLOCKED, NOT PENDING -- and this is the trap to remember. Its four cells look
like textbook mirrors (ours matches screener's con exactly; screener's std is ~40% of it).
But demerger_adj.json records a demerger effective 2025-10-15 (factor 0.459), so screener's
standalone series for pre-demerger quarters is the RESTATED continuing-operations entity,
while ours is the as-reported point-in-time figure. Writing screener's number would replace
a correct value with a restated one and look entirely plausible -- the TMPV trap. Held.
MMTC and MODIRUBBER are below this method's resolution: screener displays ~1 crore values
rounded to integers, and the reader's tolerance floor is 0.6, so 'matches screener' carries
almost no information at that magnitude. Do not grind them with this tool.
Terminal codes below are the §61 reader-failure taxonomy: the FIRST rung that broke, so an
empty result names its cause instead of standing as a conclusion.
